newsitem.title: USA: US expansion to continue - Treasury's Summers.
newsitem.headline: US expansion to continue - Treasury's Summers.

text.p: U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Laurence Summers said on Wednesday that even after two quarters of very strong economic growth, he is "confident that the expansion has a long way to run."

Speaking to reporters at a Euromoney conference, Summers noted that economic growth, which occurred at a 5.6 percent rate in the first quarter of 1997, was investment led, a fact that would help to maintain the low inflation environment.
Summers declined to comment on the dollar's actions but stressed that the U.S. unit would remain the dominant currency in the world even after the launch of the Euro.
Summers said that currency investors are rewarded on the basis of how a currency behaves and trades.
Given the depth of the U.S. market, "I expect the dollar to continue to play a prominent role in the international (monetary) system," Summers said.
He added that the impact of the Euro would "take time to play out."
